lessons.title: Commercial Exposure Without Crores: REITs, SM REITs and Fractional Platforms

children.text: Everything in the last three chapters points to one uncomfortable conclusion for most individual investors. Commercial property offers better income, but doing it well needs crores of rupees, a strong tenant, a good building, diversification across several assets and the patience to manage leases and exits. Very few people can tick all of those boxes with one purchase. The good news is that since 2019, Indian investors have been able to own slices of Grade A offices and malls through a demat account on Zerodha for the price of a single unit. This lesson compares the three main ways to get commercial exposure without buying a building: listed REITs, SM REITs and fractional ownership platforms.

body.text: You do not need to own a commercial building to own commercial rent. The trade-off is simple: you give up control, and in return you get diversification, regulation and, with listed REITs, daily liquidity.

children.text: Listed REITs: Grade A Property on the Stock Exchange

markDefs.definition: A SEBI-regulated trust that owns completed, rent-producing real estate, mostly through subsidiaries, and distributes most of its cash flow to unitholders. Its units are listed and traded on stock exchanges.

children.text: pools investor money to own completed, leased commercial property, typically large office parks or malls, and passes most of the rental cash flow to unitholders. Units trade on NSE and BSE like shares, and you can buy as little as one unit.

stats.label: Listed REITs in India
stats.context: Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield India, Nexus Select, Knowledge Realty

children.text: SEBI's rules are what make REITs suitable for ordinary investors. At least 80% of a REIT's asset value must be in completed, revenue-generating properties, which limits construction risk. At least 90% of net distributable cash flows must be paid out to unitholders, and Indian REITs typically distribute every quarter. Borrowing is capped, and the assets are valued independently and disclosed regularly.

body.label: Treated as equity since January 2026
body.context: From 1 January 2026, fresh mutual fund and SIF investments in listed REITs count as equity-related instruments, which is expected to widen institutional participation over time.

markDefs.definition: The independently assessed value of a REIT's properties minus its debt, per unit. Comparing the unit price with NAV shows whether the market is valuing the REIT at a premium or a discount to its underlying property.

children.text: If a REIT unit trades at ₹400 and distributes ₹6.50 a quarter, the annual distribution is ₹26 and the distribution yield is 6.5%. REITs also publish a
per unit, so you can see whether the market price is above or below the independently valued property underneath.

body.title: Illustrative mix of a REIT distribution
How REIT income and gains are taxed

children.text: Distributions arrive as a mix of components, each taxed differently. Interest is taxed at your slab rate. Dividends are generally exempt in your hands if the underlying company has not opted for the concessional corporate tax regime, and taxable otherwise. Repayment of debt has its own treatment and can affect the cost of your units for capital gains. Each REIT publishes the component split every quarter.

Listed REIT units held for more than 12 months produce long-term capital gains, taxed at 12.5%, and from FY 2026-27 these gains are aligned with listed equity, including the ₹1.25 lakh annual exemption. Units held for 12 months or less are taxed at 20% as short-term gains. Confirm the position with a tax professional, since REIT taxation has changed several times.

body.label: Screener.in
body.description: Search for any listed REIT, such as Embassy Office Parks REIT or Nexus Select Trust, to track its price history, distributions and financials before investing.

markDefs.definition: A SEBI-regulated REIT structure for smaller portfolios, with assets of ₹50 crore to ₹500 crore per scheme, a minimum investment of ₹10 lakh and mandatory listing of units.

children.text: For years, fractional ownership platforms let investors buy a share of a single office building or warehouse, typically for ₹10 lakh to ₹25 lakh, through a private company or LLP set up to own that asset. It was popular and largely unregulated. In March 2024, SEBI created the
framework to bring such offerings under regulation.

body.caption: SM REIT framework at a glance

cells: 200, excluding the manager and its associates
At least 95% in completed, revenue-generating property
At least 95% of net distributable cash flows
Units must be listed on a stock exchange

children.text: Property Share was among the first platforms to launch SM REIT schemes, such as PropShare Platina and PropShare Celestia, listed on BSE. The structure brings disclosure, valuation and governance standards that the old private-company model lacked.

body.text: Listed does not mean liquid. SM REIT units trade in large minimum lots and can see very little trading, so selling before the scheme exits its property may be slow or require a price discount. Most schemes also hold a single building with a handful of tenants, so one tenant leaving can hit your income hard. Treat an SM REIT as a regulated share in one property, not as a diversified REIT.

body.caption: Four routes to commercial property income

cells: Property law, RERA for new projects
One asset, one or few tenants
One unit, a few hundred rupees
High, daily on NSE and BSE

body.title: Direct ownership vs a listed REIT

columns.label: Direct commercial unit
points: You choose the asset and tenant
No manager fees, but all effort is yours
Price moves are invisible until you sell

columns.label: Listed REIT
points: Professional managers choose and run assets
Income spread across hundreds of tenants
Sell in seconds on NSE or BSE
Price moves daily with markets and interest rates

body.text: REIT prices swing more than property valuations appear to, because they are marked to market every day. A direct office unit's value also moves with interest rates and occupancy. You just do not see it until you try to sell. Daily price volatility is the visible cost of daily liquidity, not a sign that the underlying buildings are riskier.

body.title: Calculate: Your REIT Distribution Yield
body.prompt: You buy 300 units of a listed REIT at ₹375 each. Over the next year it distributes ₹24 per unit. What is your distribution yield on cost, in %?
body.explanation: Investment: 300 × ₹375 = ₹1,12,500. Annual distribution: 300 × ₹24 = ₹7,200. Yield: ₹7,200 ÷ ₹1,12,500 × 100 = 6.4%. Remember that part of this may be taxable interest and part may be tax-free dividend or repayment of debt.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: SM REIT Ticket Size
body.textWithBlank: Under SEBI's framework, the minimum investment in an SM REIT is ₹___ lakh.
body.explanation: SM REITs require a minimum of ₹10 lakh, keeping them aimed at investors who can bear the concentration and liquidity risks of a single-asset scheme.

body.title: Quick Check: Matching the Vehicle
body.question: Pooja, 29, has ₹3 lakh to invest. She wants rental income from Grade A offices, diversification across tenants, and the ability to sell if she needs the money. Which option fits best?
options: A strata office unit in Gurugram
Units of a listed REIT bought through her demat account
body.explanation: Only a listed REIT meets all three needs at her budget. A strata unit and SM REITs need far more than ₹3 lakh, and SM REITs and fractional deals are usually single-asset with limited liquidity.

body.title: Scenario: ₹50 Lakh for Commercial Income
body.scenario: Dr. Iyer, a Chennai surgeon, has ₹50 lakh set aside for commercial property income. Option A: a 600 sq ft strata office in an older OMR building leased to a local IT firm, yielding 7.5% gross. Option B: five different SM REIT schemes at ₹10 lakh each, each owning one leased office building in a different city. Option C: listed REIT units spread across three or four REITs.
body.prompt: Compare the three options on income, risk, effort and liquidity. What would you suggest?
body.modelAnswer: Option A offers the highest headline income but concentrates all ₹50 lakh in one ageing strata building with one small tenant. A single exit could cost over a year of rent, it demands his time for leases, TDS and GST, and it could take many months to sell. Option B spreads money across five buildings and cities with professional management and SEBI oversight, but each scheme is a single asset and SM REIT units may be hard to sell before the schemes exit. Option C gives exposure to Grade A campuses with hundreds of tenants, quarterly distributions, full regulation and daily liquidity on NSE and BSE, but its price will move with the market, and he has no control over the assets. For a busy surgeon who values his time, Option C, or a mix of C with one or two SM REIT schemes if he wants somewhat higher income and can hold for years, is more sensible than putting everything into Option A.

body.title: Before You Invest in an SM REIT or Fractional Deal
steps: Confirm the offering is registered under SEBI's SM REIT framework
Read the offer document: property, tenants, lease terms, lock-ins and WALE
Check who manages the scheme and their track record
Understand all fees charged by the manager
Check the planned holding period and how the property will eventually be sold
Look at trading volumes if units are listed, and assume selling early could be slow
Size it so that one tenant leaving would not damage your finances

cards.definition: A SEBI-regulated, listed trust owning completed, rent-producing property and distributing most of its cash flow.
The cash a REIT has available to pay out; at least 90% must be distributed.
Annual distribution per unit divided by unit price.
Independently valued property minus debt, per unit; the benchmark for REIT prices.
A smaller SEBI-regulated REIT scheme with ₹50 crore to ₹500 crore of assets and a ₹10 lakh minimum.
Owning a share of a single property through a pooled structure, now brought under SEBI's SM REIT framework where it qualifies.

points: India has five listed REITs with over ₹1.7 lakh crore in market value, giving access to Grade A offices and malls for the price of one unit.
SEBI requires REITs to hold mostly completed, rent-producing assets and to distribute at least 90% of distributable cash flow.
REIT distributions mix interest, dividends and repayment of debt, each taxed differently; listed units become long-term after 12 months.
SM REITs regulate fractional ownership, with a ₹10 lakh minimum and ₹50 crore to ₹500 crore of assets per scheme, but usually hold a single building.
Listed SM REIT units can still be hard to sell, so treat them as long-term, concentrated holdings.
Compare routes on ticket size, regulation, liquidity, diversification and effort, not only on headline yield.

body.text: REIT market data is as of mid-2026 and will change. Regulatory and tax rules for REITs and SM REITs have been amended several times; verify the current position before investing. Names of REITs and platforms are for illustration only. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy any security or investment product.
